templates.name: Doc Scanner — Backend (LLM Agent)
templates.description: A Python LLM agent that processes one record at a time. Watches an input folder, sends each item to a vision/text model with a structured prompt, validates the JSON response against a schema, retries on failure, and writes both a row-level CSV ledger and a per-record archive folder. The shipped baseline is a receipt scanner; the same scaffolding works for any per-record extraction or classification task.
use_cases: Receipt / invoice / form extraction from photos or PDFs
ID, license, or document field verification
Per-image classification or tagging (products, defects, content moderation)
Transcription cleanup or summarization of audio/text snippets, one file at a time
Code-file review or annotation (one file = one LLM call)
Any 'drop a file in, get a structured record out' workflow

architecture.launcher: run_app.sh / run_app.bat (cd into the folder, python app.py)

key_files.role: Orchestrator. Watches document_input/, dispatches files to a worker thread pool, coordinates logging.
Builds the system + user prompt from instructions.json and output_schema.json, base64-encodes images, calls the LLM.
Wraps the LLM call. Re-asks on missing fields or network errors; exponential backoff on 429s.
Appends the validated record to classifications.csv. Thread-safe under concurrent writes.
Copies the original input and the JSON record into agent_results/scanned/{record_id}/ for audit.
Prompt configuration: system text, per-field rules, model choice, max_retries.
JSON Schema (strict) that the LLM output must match. Drives both validation and prompt generation.

architecture.data_flow: document_input/{file} → prompt.py builds request → LLM call (with retry.py) → parse.py appends row to agent_results/classifications.csv → export.py archives a copy under agent_results/scanned/{record_id}/

edit: instructions.json — change the system prompt, per-field rules, model, max_retries
output_schema.json — change the fields the LLM must return (and any enums that drive the prompt)

env.OPENAI_API_KEY: Required. Lives in .env next to run_app.sh.
env.IMAGE_SCANNER_WORKERS: Optional. Worker thread count (default tuned for typical desktops).

templates.name: Dashboard PWA — DuckDB-WASM
templates.description: A Progressive Web App that runs entirely in the browser. The user's data ships as Parquet files; DuckDB-WASM executes SQL client-side; React (loaded as a UMD bundle, no npm) renders a dataset picker, filterable table, and pagination. The output is a self-contained folder with a launcher per OS — zip it, hand it to anyone, and it works with no Python, no Node, and no install.
use_cases: Interactive sales / KPI dashboards over a snapshot of company data
Survey-result or research-data browsers shared with non-technical collaborators
Read-only data explorers for journalism, civic data, or public reports
Log or event-stream slicers built from a periodic export
Catalog browsers (products, papers, datasets) with faceted filtering
Any 'I want to share an interactive view of this dataset' app where the data fits in the browser

architecture.runtime: Browser (modern, WASM-capable). Python 3 only used at build time, not by end users.
architecture.entry_point: run_app.sh (dev) → prepare_dev_assets.py + serve.py. build_app_package.py produces the distributable.
architecture.launcher: run_app.sh / run_app.bat for dev; output_folder/{app}/mac_start.command, mac_start.sh, pc_start.bat for end users.

key_files.role: Build script. Stages parquets from input_folder/, copies src_app/ to output_folder/, writes the end-user launcher trio.
Dev helper. Syncs the parquets listed in app_config.json from input_folder/ into src_app/data/. Idempotent.
Local HTTP server for development. Picks a free port, registers .wasm and .parquet MIME types, opens the browser.
Static shell. Loads React UMD, the DuckDB bundle, and js/app.js.
React app (no JSX). Boots DuckDB-WASM, loads parquets, renders the dataset picker, filters, and table.
App configuration: title and dataset list. Each dataset declares its file and the filter type per column (select / text / range / boolean).
Pre-bundled React 18, ReactDOM 18, and DuckDB-WASM (bundle + .wasm + worker). Committed so users don't need npm.
Recipe. Tells the student which files to edit when forking and which to leave alone. Delete it after cloning.

architecture.data_flow: input_folder/*.parquet → prepare_dev_assets stages into src_app/data/ → browser fetches at runtime → DuckDB-WASM registers as a virtual file → SQL queries with filters + LIMIT/OFFSET → React table render

edit: app_core/src_app/data/app_config.json — dataset list and per-column filter types
delete_after_cloning: any sample parquets shipped in src_app/data/

templates.name: Doc Scanner — Fullstack (React + Flask)
templates.description: A two-process app: a React frontend (Vite) talks to a Flask backend over /api/*. The shipped baseline wraps the Track 4 receipt-scanner agent in HTTP — the backend exposes upload + list + detail endpoints, streams scan progress over Server-Sent Events, and the frontend renders tables and an image preview. Use this when an app needs a live server at runtime (secrets, external APIs, mutations, auth, long-running jobs).
use_cases: Web UI on top of an LLM agent so non-technical users can drop files in and see results stream back
Internal admin tools that hit external APIs (CRMs, payment processors, vendor portals)
RAG / semantic-search front ends backed by a local vector store and embeddings calls
Workflow apps that mutate state (mark records reviewed, approve, re-run) and need a server to hold it
Anything requiring auth, API keys, or secrets that can't live in the browser
Long-running batch jobs where the UI needs live progress updates

architecture.runtime: Python 3.8+ (backend) and Node.js 16+ (frontend dev server). Modern browser.
architecture.entry_point: setup.sh (one-time install) then run_app.sh (launch both servers).
architecture.launcher: setup.sh / setup.bat for first-run install; run_app.sh / run_app.bat to launch backend + frontend concurrently on auto-picked ports; clear_cache.sh / clear_cache.bat for a clean rebuild.

key_files.role: Idempotent first-run install. pip installs backend deps, npm installs frontend deps.
Reserves two free ports (BACKEND_PORT, FRONTEND_PORT), launches Flask + Vite concurrently.
Removes node_modules, __pycache__, and build artifacts, then re-runs setup.
Flask app. Endpoints: POST /api/scan (multipart upload → SSE stream), GET /api/receipts, GET /api/line_items, GET /api/receipts/<id>/items, GET /api/image/<id>.
Verbatim role-named modules from the doc_scanner_backend template. Same retry, schema validation, and archive logic, now driven by HTTP requests instead of a folder watcher.
Prompt configuration for the wrapped agent.
JSON Schema the LLM output must match.
Backend Python deps.
React UI. Upload form, SSE stream consumer, receipt + line-item tables, detail drawer with image preview.
Reads FRONTEND_PORT and BACKEND_PORT env vars; proxies /api to the backend.
Frontend deps: react, react-dom, vite, @vitejs/plugin-react.

architecture.data_flow: Browser upload → POST /api/scan (multipart) → Flask saves to backend/document_input/ → worker thread pool runs the per-file agent (prompt → LLM → retry → parse) → results appended to backend/agent_results/classifications.csv and archived under backend/agent_results/scanned/{id}/ → SSE event per completed record → frontend tables update live.

edit_for_ui: frontend/src/App.jsx and any sibling React components
do_not_edit: the role-named .py filenames in backend/ (preserve prompt.py / parse.py / retry.py / export.py)

env.OPENAI_API_KEY: Required. Lives in .env next to run_app.sh.
env.BACKEND_PORT: Set automatically by run_app.sh; do not hardcode.
env.FRONTEND_PORT: Set automatically by run_app.sh; do not hardcode.

notes: backend/document_input/ and backend/agent_results/ live inside the app folder, not at project-level input_folder/ or output_folder/. This keeps the app self-contained when zipped and shared.
